correctness.rationale: The source definitions give \(q_n\), \(r_n\), \(N_n\), \(M_n\), \(P_n\) and the canonical digit spectrum. Mixed-radix reduction proves \(\#\Lambda_n=\prod_{j\le n}M_j\) exactly. The extremal digit sum gives \(4P_n/9\le R_n<27P_n/52\). Spacing \(P_nh_{n+1}>3P_n\) isolates stages. The source growth \(N_{n+1}>P_n^{\,n+1}\) implies last-scale logarithmic domination. These facts prove completed-stage exponent \(s\), gap-subsequence exponent \(0\), and a uniform between-stage upper bound with endpoint exponent \(s\). The proof explicitly excludes \(s=1\).

value.rationale: The primary source introduces the first singular Salem spectral measures on the real line. The exact pair \(\left(0,s\right)\) exposes a natural and pronounced intermittency of the canonical orthonormal basis: it reaches the geometric Salem exponent on completed stages yet has arbitrarily deep sparse logarithmic gaps. This distinguishes global centered growth from more translation-flexible density invariants and is structurally motivated by the new construction.
